items.title: Existence of the universal first order thickening of a formally unramified morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that a formally unramified morphism h : Z to X admits a first order thickening Z in Z' that is universal for all diagrams T in T' over X (statement lines 1026-1028), an object defined by a lifting property rather than constructed by a formula. The proof is a construction with a chain of genuinely separate steps: it first derives uniqueness and the localisation of the universal property for open subschemes from the definition (proof lines 1040-1061), then upgrades the algebra lemma from affine test diagrams to arbitrary ones by an affine open covering of T' and a glueing with uniqueness (proof lines 1063-1081), then produces the global Z' by glueing affine pieces along open subschemes that are identified as universal thickenings of the intersections, which is what yields the cocycle condition (proof lines 1083-1101). The final and least formal step is the descent of the universal property itself: local universality on a cover of Z has to be converted into the lifting property for an arbitrary diagram, which is done by covering T' so that each a(T_i) lands in some Z_i and then comparing two solutions through the universal thickening of Z_i cap Z_j (proof lines 1108-1126). Formal unramifiedness is consumed at exactly one point, proof line 1086.
